note: Local scanned books used for the cross-book skew survey. Paths beginning with ~ are expanded at run time; the survey records each PDF's SHA-256. Descriptions are from file names and visible page content only.

books.description: Kale (1913), the project's test book: Sanskrit verses with Sanskrit commentary and footnotes; Google Books scan, 600 dpi bilevel page images.

Digital Library of India scan (dli.granth.78136) of a Telang edition of Bhartrhari: Sanskrit verses with a small-type variant-reading apparatus and English notes; 1500 x 2500 pixel grayscale or RGB page images.
Vavilla edition with the Ramachandra Budhendra commentary: Sanskrit verses with Sanskrit prose commentary and numbered notes; 600 dpi bilevel page images.
The Nitisataka, Sringarasataka and Vairagyasataka (1896), Google Books XikpAAAAYAAJ: large-type Sanskrit verse, Hindi and English translation, footnotes; 600 dpi grayscale.
The Nitisataka, Sringarasataka and Vairagyasataka (1914), Google Books VeBjAAAAMAAJ: same layout family as the 1896 edition; 600 dpi grayscale.
books.caveat: Pages have a border of small repeated ornaments. The line segmentation attaches ornament components to text lines, so this book's line-pair statistics are not reliable. Page angles are unaffected in inspection.

books.description: M. N. Dutt's English Mahabharata, per-chapter PDFs: two columns, each interleaving Devanagari verses with English translation; 300 dpi bilevel page images.
F. N. Cole, Bulletin of the AMS (1903), Project Euclid scan: English mathematical prose with displayed formulas and a footnote; 600 dpi bilevel.
